15.history: The harbour of the red strait keeps the orthodox rite of Brìde's flame. Its house of Brìde bought two years' altar coal ahead in the sixth year, lest the coal fail before the rite did, and burned the last of it in the eighteenth. Its boats carried the regiments' bread along the coast in the column's year, a soldier aboard each to count the loaves, and its harbour victualled the garrisons and An dàrna cabhlach through the war; for that it was granted in {{year:VI-0120a}} a market right for the southern strait, the sixteenth market town and the last chartered. Its first market under the charter was held in the rain on the quay.
15.known_for: its rite of Brìde's flame and the last market charter

86.history: The salt-pan town of the low strait on the north coast tried the northern cake under one of its pans in the fourth year and found it boiled the brine as well as coal. In the war a clerk of An t-Ionmhas sat at the pump by the pans to take the tithe, and the salt-boilers said salt paid twice. Its forge smelts the bog-iron of the district, and in {{year:VI-0132a}} took the kingdom's contract for the regiments' small arms; the woman who keeps it took on four boys and a girl to answer it. The pans are boiled with dubhan now, bought at the pump An t-Ionmhas's clerk sits beside, and the salt of Caol ìseal goes east and west along the north coast in engine-boats of Caol mhòr's fitting.
86.known_for: its salt pans and its forge

286.history: The small town of the harbour carts in the Cuan shean shire blesses its carts every spring, horses and all, and in the seventh year its priest held a dubhan lamp on a tail-board blessed because it was on the cart. Its forges smelt the bog-iron of the district, and in {{year:VI-0132a}} took the contract for the regiments' small arms and field-guns with Caol ìseal, the forge-towns of the old vein country following; a smith of the town counts his musket-stocks by the hundred. The town lies on the harbour road of the Cuan shean shire, where the carts of An ceathramh cabhlach's harbour go up and down all day; since the war its forges work by dubhan heat, and the blessing of the carts at the spring draws the regiments' own wagoners to stand with their teams among the town's.
286.known_for: its blessing of the harbour carts, and its forges

7001.name: Freiceadan Àth leathan
7001.history: The post of An seachdamh rèisimeid on the road below Àth leathan was built in the autumn of the year after the war, when the western seams had been capped with the regiment standing by at every capping. It keeps a company there, whose patrols pass the cairn on the field and leave it standing. The regimental lists call it Freiceadan Àth leathan; the town calls it something else, which the lists do not give. Its men spent their first winter roofing it with slates bought at the western Seann Skell. The last holdouts of the hills came down to An seachdamh rèisimeid's posts on this road to give up their arms.
7001.known_for: An seachdamh rèisimeid's post, called something else in the town
